questions.q: When plotting a line graph of enzyme activity against temperature, which axis should conventionally display the temperature values?

The vertical y-axis

The diagonal grid corners

questions.q: On a standard biological graph, what must be included on both the x-axis and y-axis labels?
a: Only the name of the variable
The variable name followed by a forward slash and its SI unit (e.g., Rate / cm³ min⁻¹)
The raw numerical data points

a: To make the graph look colorful and artistic
To fit as many numbers as possible into a tiny space
To ensure that data points are distributed accurately and proportional distances are maintained

a: It should occupy a tiny corner so there is room for writing notes

When the data points are completely random and unrelated

questions.q: How should an obvious anomalous data point be treated when drawing a line of best fit on a graph?
a: Bend the line sharply so it touches every single error
Erase it from the data table permanently
Ignore the anomaly when drawing the smooth line of best fit, as it represents experimental error
Connect it with a bright red dashed line

a: Multiply the maximum y value by the minimum x value
Add all coordinates together and divide by two
Count the total number of grid squares on the page
Divide the change in y by the change in x (Delta y / Delta x) using a large triangle spanning over half the line

questions.q: When should a bar chart be drawn instead of a continuous line graph?
a: When the independent variable is categorical, discrete, or discontinuous (e.g., different types of plant fertilizers)
When plotting continuous numerical time against temperature
When data has no numerical values whatsoever
When showing exponential population growth

questions.q: What is the primary rule regarding the spacing of bars on a bar chart comparing discrete categories?
a: Bars must overlap each other by 50 percent
Equal spaces must be left between adjacent bars
Bars must be placed on opposite sides of the page margin
There must be zero gaps between any bars

questions.q: What is a histogram used for, and how does it differ fundamentally from a bar chart?
a: Histograms show animal pictures; bar charts show plant structures
Histograms are drawn in colored pens; bar charts in pencil
Histograms display continuous grouped numerical data where bars touch with no spaces, representing frequency distributions

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of plotting data into a graphical format rather than leaving it in a data table?
a: To make the practical report heavier
To hide incorrect equipment readings
To use up extra stationery
To reveal underlying trends, patterns, correlations, and anomalies visually that raw numbers may obscure

questions.q: When interpolating data from a graph line, what are you doing?
a: Estimating an unknown value that lies *between* actually measured data points on the graph

Calculating the average of all table rows

questions.q: What is extrapolation on a graph?
a: Reading a value directly between two plotted points
Extending the line of best fit beyond the range of measured experimental data to predict unmeasured values
Erasing incorrect points from the axis
Measuring the angle of the slope with a protractor

questions.q: Why is a title essential for every graph constructed in an IGCSE biology report?

To give the graph a decorative name
To state clearly what the graph displays, usually linking the dependent variable to the independent variable
To indicate the student's grade

questions.q: If a graph line of enzyme activity against substrate concentration plateaus (levels off) at high substrate concentrations, what does this indicate?

The reaction has reversed direction

questions.q: What does a negative correlation on a scatter graph indicate about two variables?

As one variable increases, the other variable also increases
There is zero mathematical relationship between them
Both variables remain completely constant

questions.q: What does a positive correlation on a graph signify?
a: The experiment was a complete failure
As the independent variable increases, the dependent variable also increases
As time increases, the temperature drops to absolute zero
The variables are inversely proportional

questions.q: What does it mean if a graph line shows a flat horizontal plateau where the gradient is zero?
a: The dependent variable is increasing exponentially
The rate of reaction has doubled
The dependent variable is no longer changing as the independent variable increases
The equipment has completely melted

questions.q: When calculating percentage increase from graph data values, which formula is correct?
a: (Original value minus new value) divided by new value multiplied by 100
New value multiplied by original value divided by 10
New value plus original value divided by two
((New value minus original value) divided by original value) multiplied by 100

questions.q: Why should a line of best fit be a single thin, crisp line rather than a thick, hairy, or sketched line?

Examiners cannot see thick lines

questions.q: What is a pie chart best used for when representing biological data?

questions.q: When interpreting a graph showing population growth of bacteria over time, what does the steep exponential phase indicate?

questions.q: What is the correct term for data that can take any numerical value within a given range (such as length, mass, or temperature)?

Categorical data
Attribute data

questions.q: What type of data is represented by categories that cannot be measured numerically on a continuous scale (e.g., eye color, blood group, or plant species)?

Interpolated data

questions.q: If a graph has a non-linear scale (e.g., logarithmic intervals), what major risk does this introduce if misinterpreted?
